summary: Creates an IANA registry for parameters and values used in tel URIs, and fills it with the parameters from the tel URI specification and from extensions for number portability and trunk groups. It updates RFC 3966 and is on the standards track.

eli5.summary: This is an official list of the extra settings you can add to a telephone-number link, so everyone uses the same names for them.

questions: what is the tel uri parameter registry
how do i register a new tel uri parameter
what parameters does the tel uri support
subtitle: A standard registry for the settings used in telephone-number links.

tldr.problem: RFC 3966 defined the tel URI format for representing telephone numbers, but did not specify how new extensions and parameters would be registered in a central place.
tldr.mechanism: This RFC creates an IANA registry for tel URI parameters and fills it with parameters from the original tel URI spec and extensions for number portability and trunk groups.
tldr.outcome: New tel URI extensions must now be formally registered with IANA to ensure interoperability and prevent name collisions.

today: RFC 5341 created an IANA registry for tel URI parameters that is still used today. New parameters and parameter values for tel URIs must now be formally registered through IANA to be considered standardized.

sections.title: Introduction
sections.content:
The tel URI, defined in RFC 3966, provides a way to represent telephone numbers as web-style links. Like many other URIs, the tel scheme supports extensibility: you can add new parameters and new values to customize how a telephone number is used.

However, RFC 3966 did not specify where these parameters should be registered or managed. Without a central registry, different groups might invent the same parameter name for different purposes, or use conflicting syntax. This RFC creates an IANA registry to solve that problem and fills it with the parameters already defined in tel URI extensions.
sections.eli5: A tel URI is like a phone number link on the web. But if lots of people want to add their own special settings to it, they need an official place to register those settings so they don't step on each other.

sections.title: The tel URI Concept
sections.content:
A tel URI is a Uniform Resource Identifier that identifies a resource by a telephone number. It lets applications create clickable telephone numbers that can trigger calling, messaging, or other phone-based actions. The format is simple: tel:+1-201-555-0123 is a valid tel URI.

The tel scheme supports parameters, which are optional additions that provide extra information or modify the meaning of the number. For example, an extension might specify a phone context or a routing preference. These parameters use the query-string style syntax common in URIs.
sections.eli5: A tel URI is a computer-friendly way to write a phone number as a link. You can add extra information to that link, like what company it's for or where it should be routed.

sections.title: The Parameter Registry
sections.content:
The tel URI Parameter Registry is a table where each registered parameter has a name, a description of what values it accepts, and a reference to the RFC or specification that defines it.

Some parameters take predefined values (marked as "Constrained"), where the specification lists the valid options. Some parameters take no value at all and work as flags. Others accept any value. The registry indicates which type each parameter is, so implementors know what to expect.
sections.eli5: The registry is a list that says what extra settings can be added to a tel URI and what kinds of values they accept.

sections.title: Registration Requirements
sections.content:
To register a new parameter or parameter value with IANA, the specification must be documented in an RFC or other permanent and publicly available specification. The documentation must fully explain the syntax, intended usage, and semantics of the parameter.

This requirement ensures that independent implementations can interoperate correctly and prevents accidental namespace collisions. When registering a new value for an existing parameter, you must reference the specification that provides that value. The registration policy is "Specification Required, Designated Expert": a technical expert reviews all requests to ensure they meet the standards for interoperability and do not conflict with existing registrations.
sections.eli5: Before you can add a new setting to the registry, you have to write down exactly what it does in a document that everyone can see. A technical expert then checks it to make sure it won't cause problems.

sections.title: Initial Parameters
sections.content:
The RFC populates the registry with twelve initial parameters, sourced from the tel URI specification and from extensions for number portability and trunk groups.

Parameters from the base tel URI specification include isub (ISDN subaddress), isub-encoding (how the subaddress is encoded), ext (extension), and phone-context (context for the number). Extensions for number portability add npdi (Number Portability Dip Indicator, a flag), rn (routing number), rn-context, cic (Carrier Identification Code), and cic-context. Extensions for trunk groups add tgrp (trunk group) and trunk-context. Each entry in the registry references the RFC that defines it.
sections.eli5: The registry starts with twelve settings that are already used by phone number links: things like extensions, context information, and special codes for handling number portability.

sections.title: Security Considerations
sections.content:
The registry itself does not have direct security implications. However, any new parameter registered must be reviewed for security considerations by the RFC that proposes it. Each specification defining a new parameter MUST provide detailed security analysis for how that parameter could be misused or how its presence or absence could affect the security of the system processing the tel URI.

This ensures that the IETF reviews security impacts before parameters are standardized, preventing insecure parameters from being widely adopted.
sections.eli5: The registry doesn't have its own security problems, but every new setting that gets registered has to explain if it could cause any security issues.

sections.title: Status Today
sections.content: RFC 3966 remains the current specification for tel URIs, and RFC 5341 updates it to add the formal registry. The registry is maintained by IANA and continues to accept new parameter registrations that meet the "Specification Required, Designated Expert" policy.
sections.eli5: RFC 5341 created the official list for tel URI settings, and that list is still being used today whenever someone wants to add a new setting to a phone number link.
